name: Apollo 11 (Mare Tranquillitatis)
notes: First crewed Moon landing; flat basaltic mare with direct Earth line-of-sight.

name: Apollo 12 (Oceanus Procellarum)
notes: Precision landing next to Surveyor 3; flat volcanic plain.

name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro Highlands)
notes: Rolling ejecta blanket from the Imbrium impact basin.

name: Apollo 15 (Hadley-Apennine)
notes: First Lunar Roving Vehicle site; bordered by steep Apennine mountains and Hadley Rille.

name: Apollo 16 (Descartes Highlands)
notes: Ancient cratered lunar highlands with higher terrain roughness.

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow Valley)
notes: Deep valley floor flanked by tall massifs; rich geological diversity.

name: Mons Mouton (Artemis III)
notes: Flat-topped South Pole mountain plateau with high solar exposure and water-ice access.

name: Malapert Massif (Artemis III)
notes: Elevated ridge offering strong Earth communications and sustained sunlight.

name: Nobile Rim 1 (Artemis III)
notes: Western rim of Nobile Crater adjacent to large permanently shadowed regions (PSRs).

name: Nobile Rim 2 (Artemis III)
notes: High-value scientific terrain along Nobile Crater's outer rim.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2 (Artemis III)
notes: Very close to the South Pole with near-continuous solar peaks and nearby ice traps.

name: Haworth Region (Artemis III)
notes: Borders Haworth Crater, one of the coldest water-ice cold traps on the Moon.

name: Slater Plain (Artemis III)
notes: Relatively smooth polar plain offering safer touchdown geometry near the South Pole.

name: Peak Near Cabeus B (Artemis III)
notes: Located near Cabeus Crater, where LCROSS confirmed subsurface water ice.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti Point)
notes: First soft landing in the southern high-latitude highlands.

name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán Crater)
notes: First lunar far-side landing; requires a relay satellite for Earth communication.

name: Chang'e 5 (Mons Rümker)
notes: Sample return from geologically young volcanic mare in northern Oceanus Procellarum.

name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo Basin - Far Side)
notes: First lunar far-side sample return inside the South Pole-Aitken basin.

name: Luna 24 (Mare Crisium)
notes: Smooth eastern mare basin; returned deep regolith core samples.

name: JAXA SLIM (Shioli Crater)
notes: Pinpoint landing test on a steep crater rim slope.
